own_solution.law: Kirchhoff's loop law gives RC dVC/dt + VC = V0. With VC(0)=0, VC(t)=V0[1-exp(-t/(RC))]. Here RC=0.100 s and VC(0.080 s)=12[1-exp(-0.8)]. An additional series resistance q replaces R by R+q. Opening the charging loop at time q gives VC(t)=V0[1-exp(-min(t,q)/(RC))], with times expressed in seconds.
assumptions: The resistor and capacitor obey the standard lumped, constant-parameter circuit model.
The capacitor is initially uncharged and does not leak, as stated.
The batteries and wires are ideal, as stated.
Opening the charging loop provides no discharge path.
The lamp and second battery form a separate circuit.

T6DDA.regime: The disconnection occurs at or after the 80 ms observation time.

T83CD.regime: The switch opens at or after the 80 ms observation time.

notes: The authors' claims agree with the locked pass-1 review. Using SI conversions, the additional series resistances 1.5, 3.5 and 7 kΩ give approximately 5.514792, 4.504383 and 3.401624 V, respectively. Opening at 30 and 60 ms gives approximately 3.110181 and 5.414260 V. Every listed K time exceeds 80 ms and every listed early-opening time is below it. Equality at 80 ms also gives the base voltage by continuity; the authors' strict boundary convention affects no listed value. The separate lamp circuit and the completed earlier experiment introduce no dependency on the target. Both declared minimal pairs preserve the number and unit while changing the intended attachment. Both numeral-free controls match their stated twins after replacing the resistance phrase. All certified answers have adequate numerical precision. No revision of pass 1 is needed.
